xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4791: PAN-4777 follow-up: CodeRabbit findings on #4789 (cleanup-promise scope in fly-provider.md, volume cleanup in recovery text)

plan.title: PAN-4777 follow-up: CodeRabbit findings on #4789 (cleanup-promise scope in fly-provider.md, volume cleanup in recovery text)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: CodeRabbit left two Minor findings on PR #4789 (PAN-4777) that merged unanswered. (1) docs/fly-provider.md promises that any failure after the Fly machine is created deletes it, but a failure while createVm waits for 'started' rejects before the rollback try block, so the machine (and a durable-tier volume) stays. The same doc states the startup wait as 120 s where the code waits 300 s. (2) When rollBackVm's delete fails, its recovery text tells the operator to destroy only the machine; on the durable tier the <vmName>-workspace volume also survives and keeps billing.
narratives.Proposal: WI-1 rewrites docs/fly-provider.md so automatic cleanup is promised only for setup steps that run after the create step (createVm) returns, says a create-step failure such as the 300 s startup wait leaves the machine (found with fly machines list -a <app>, recovered by re-running pan workspace create --remote <issue> or destroyed by hand), says rollback only tries to delete the durable volume and tells durable operators to check fly volumes list, and corrects 120 s to 300 s. WI-2 makes rollBackVm's recovery text tier-aware via fly.getResiliencyTier(): on 'durable' it appends fly volumes list / fly volumes destroy <volume-id> --yes after the machine destroy; ephemeral text is unchanged. Each item ends by replying on its own CodeRabbit thread with the pushed fix commit SHA.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing createVm to delete a machine or durable volume when createMachine or the startup wait fails
- Changing deleteVm's silent swallow of a volume-delete error
- Writing a user-facing page for the durable resiliency tier
- Any change to src/lib/remote/fly-provider.ts, src/lib/remote/fly-api.ts, or src/lib/anywhere/fly/
- Changing the ephemeral-tier recovery text

autoDecisions.summary: Narrow the doc promise instead of adding cleanup inside createVm.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks to 'limit the cleanup promise'; deleting a machine that may still be pulling its image is a behavior change with its own risks and belongs in a separate issue.

autoDecisions.summary: Recovery text adds volume steps only when fly.getResiliencyTier() === 'durable'.
autoDecisions.rationale: Only the durable tier attaches a <vmName>-workspace volume; telling ephemeral operators to hunt a volume that cannot exist is noise. getResiliencyTier() already exists on FlyProvider (fly-provider.ts line 115).

autoDecisions.summary: Correct the Fly startup wait from 120 s to 300 s at docs/fly-provider.md lines 62, 257, 447.
autoDecisions.rationale: The rewritten text describes the startup-wait failure; leaving a wrong figure beside it would be a new defect. Code waits 300 s for fresh and adopted machines.

autoDecisions.summary: Thread replies cite the pushed fix commit SHA and PAN-4791 rather than the PR URL; each item replies on its own thread.
autoDecisions.rationale: Items must complete before pan done opens the PR, so the PR URL does not exist yet; GitHub cross-links the issue to the PR. Each CodeRabbit thread maps to exactly one item, so no extra edge is needed.

autoDecisions.summary: Recovery after a create-step failure is re-running pan workspace create --remote <issue> (adopts the leftover machine) or fly machines destroy; never pan workspace start.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plan critic round 1: startCommand refuses issues with no saved metadata, and metadata is saved only after creation succeeds.

autoDecisions.summary: Doc says rollback tries to delete the durable volume and tells operators to check fly volumes list, instead of promising deletion.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plan critic round 1: deleteVm swallows volume errors; changing that is a NonGoal, so the doc must not over-promise.

items.title: Bound the Fly cleanup promise in docs/fly-provider.md to post-createVm setup failures and correct the startup wait to 300 s

expected_outputs: first command exits 0 (no 120 s figure remains)
the Machine not started bullet contains 'pan workspace create --remote <issue>' and no 'pan workspace start'
fourth command prints at least one line in the troubleshooting section

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1 exactly (.pan/drafts/PAN-4791.md, including its Critique response). Edit docs/fly-provider.md: line 62 '120 s' -> '300 s'; line 67 setup bullet -> 'If a setup step after the create step fails (credential sync onward), delete the machine and try to delete its durable-tier volume before reporting the error. If the create step itself fails (for example the machine does not reach `started` within 300 s), the machine is left in place; find it with `fly machines list -a <app>`.' Never phrase the boundary as 'after the machine reaches started': createVm can still fail after the wait (getMachine). Line 257 'up to 120 seconds.' -> 'up to 300 seconds.'; lines 447-448 'Machine not started' bullet -> 300 s, the machine is not deleted, find it with fly machines list, re-run `pan workspace create --remote <issue>` to adopt and start it or destroy it by hand; remove the `pan workspace start <issue>` instruction (it refuses issues with no saved metadata). Lines 458-463: rename heading to '**Creation fails during setup**', open with any failure in a setup step after the create step returns, keep the step list and the #4748 sentence, say volume deletion is attempted (not guaranteed), and end with the machine-destroy command followed by: on the durable tier run `fly volumes list -a <app>` after any failed creation; if a `<vm-name>-workspace` volume is still listed, destroy it with `fly volumes destroy <volume-id> -a <app> --yes`. Do not touch line 281 (pan workspace start for a stopped, already-created workspace is correct there). Commit with trailer 'Item: wi1-docs', push, then post exactly one reply: gh api -X POST repos/eltmon/overdeck/pulls/4789/comments/4438995645/replies -f body='Fixed in <sha> for #4791: ...' (body text in PRD WI-1 step 6).
